title: chest (anterior and lateral thorax)

chart.description: The front and sides of the thorax unrolled round a horizontal section of the skin. u: arc length (cm) from the anterior median line, positive towards the patient's LEFT, as far as the mid-axillary lines. v: height (cm) above the xiphisternal junction. d: depth below the skin along the inward normal (cm).

structures.label: ascending aorta and arch (behind the sternum)

description: The anterior chest wall is skin, subcutaneous fat and breast tissue, pectoral and intercostal muscles over the ribs; the parietal pleura lies just inside it, closest in the intercostal spaces and where the wall is thin (slim build, laterally). Left of the lower sternum the heart lies directly behind the wall (the cardiac notch); low on the right the liver lies under the diaphragm behind the costodiaphragmatic recess. The internal thoracic vessels run about a finger's breadth lateral to the sternal edge. The sternum stops a perpendicular needle; a congenital sternal foramen may lie under CV17.

sources.note: For what the reference body does not contain (ribs and intercostal spaces, sternum, scapulae, nerves, peripheral vessels, the fat/muscle split of the body wall): topography only, no third-party geometry or images.

review.notes: Depths below the skin of the lungs, organs, bones and great vessels are measured on one reference body (a 38-year-old man of about 90 kg) and scaled to each patient by height and BMI; the rest is schematic. Not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.

provenance.notes: Depth grid (2 cm): skin-to-pleura and skin-to-organ distances measured by rays on the reference body; the fat/muscle split of the wall, the sternum and the intercostal-space levels are schematic. Ribs are not modelled: every non-sternal location is treated as an intercostal space (the conservative case).
